question.name: CSEC Bio May 2022 Q6d(i) — State Two Sexually Transmitted Diseases
question.general_feedback:
Sexually Transmitted Diseases (STDs):

Any TWO of the following:

  • Gonorrhoea — bacterial STD caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae; causes discharge and burning urination
  • Syphilis — bacterial STD caused by Treponema pallidum; progresses in stages
  • Chlamydia — bacterial STD; often asymptomatic; can cause infertility
  • HIV/AIDS — viral STD; attacks the immune system; no cure, managed with antiretroviral drugs
  • Genital Herpes — viral STD caused by Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV-2)

Prevention: Condoms are the only barrier method that protects against both pregnancy and STDs.

groups.label: First sexually transmitted disease (STD)
groups.diagnostic_hint: STDs are infections spread primarily through sexual contact. CSEC-expected examples include Gonorrhoea, Syphilis, Chlamydia, HIV/AIDS, and Genital Herpes. Malaria and Dengue are vector-borne, not sexually transmitted.

groups.label: Second sexually transmitted disease (different from first)
groups.diagnostic_hint: Name a second, different STD. Malaria is transmitted by mosquitoes and Dengue by Aedes mosquitoes — neither is an STD.

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 7 tokens for 2 slots. 5 correct STDs — student picks any 2. 'Malaria' is a Caribbean-context trap: it is a significant disease in the region but is transmitted by mosquitoes (Anopheles), not sexually. 'Dengue fever' is also mosquito-borne (Aedes aegypti) — very common in Caribbean countries, making it a plausible but incorrect distractor for Caribbean students.
